summary: Preserved PR 843's fatal accelerator classification and restart-required response, but replaced scheduler exit with a latched fatal state so subsequent requests fail immediately without GPU dispatch instead of blocking on an absent scheduler.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: the candidate stopped its RPC event loop after the fatal reply, violating the probe's requirement that later requests receive a fail-fast response.
Passing-after: fatal state remained reachable over RPC and a later request was rejected without invoking its worker handler.
34 focused unit tests passed, covering fatal classification/state, nonfatal boundaries, shutdown dispatch, RPC timeout behavior, warmup degradation, and worker shutdown.

gpu_execution.evidence: The correction is scheduler control-flow behavior and was reproduced deterministically without model execution. No claim is made about the unavailable CUDA workload.

remaining_limitations: The RTX 5070 12 GB / WSL2 / CUDA 13.0 MiniMax-H3 workload, model weights, and reporter LoRA were unavailable on the prepared ROCm 7.2 system.
The initial 1344x768 failure was not proven to be resource exhaustion, so no insufficient-memory relabeling or resolution admission threshold was added.
Disaggregated role event loops use separate transport and exception paths; equivalent fatal-state behavior was not changed or claimed without a qualified reproduction.
